# Feature: Proxy-side proactive session compaction (Tier 1)

**STATUS: DEFERRED — implementation delayed until client-side compaction
results are available.** Client-side compaction machinery is now in place in
ContextHub (Compact-and-Continue WL-0MR269PDV00970YP, auto-continue
WL-0MSMGGPWR000MZ0O; gate-response wiring WL-0MTBOXEGR009KDP6). Per
operator decision (2026-08-28), server-side compaction must not be
implemented until results from the client-side effort are reviewed; this
item is parked (status `blocked`) pending that review.

Implementation of the F4 recommendation (LP-0MTC8BWV50012WSW,
`docs/session-compaction-recommendations.md`) within the two-tier scheme of
LP-0MTCW79RR000LFMJ. The proxy compacts the session at **prompt-assembly
time** when estimated tokens exceed the trigger — no round trip, no
client-side coordination.

## Behavior (both modes — Strategy C, summarize-first)

Per operator decision (2026-08-28), serve-side compaction uses the hybrid
Strategy C in **both** fast and cheap modes, with the **first prompt always
retained verbatim**.

### Retention invariant (fast AND cheap)

The compacted prompt MUST always contain, unchanged:

1. the system prompt;
2. the **very first user prompt** (the original task statement/setup, which
   carries essential instructions);
3. the most recent turns within budget.

Everything between the first prompt and the recent window is folded into a
summary injected at the top of the prompt (below the retained first prompt).

### Fast mode — Strategy C

- **Trigger:** `estimated_tokens > 58,300` (= 0.70 × per-slot clamp 83,285).
  Fires before the existing `context_pressure_warn_ratio` (0.8 × 83,285 =
  66.6K) so compaction is proactive, not reactive.
- **Target:** compacted prompt ≤ 38,000 tokens (`local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold`,
  fast profile): retain system prompt + first prompt + recent turns; fold
  the rest into a summary.
- **Backstop:** only if the session still exceeds budget after summarizing,
  drop oldest non-first turns (whole turns, never splittable, never the
  system prompt or first prompt), logged.
- **Automatic** on breach.

### Cheap mode — Strategy C (hybrid)

- **Trigger:** `estimated_tokens > 43,000` (= 0.70 × static clamp 61,440).
- **Target:** compacted prompt ≤ 30,000 tokens: same retention invariant +
  summary of the middle.
- **Non-compactable** (summarizer unavailable, or still over budget after
  compaction): route remote with guidance — never silent remote fallback,
  never near-full-slot local prefill (LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D AC4).
- **Automatic** on breach.

## Implementation approach

- **Trigger hook:** reuse the existing `context_pressure` machinery in
  `proxy/provider.py` (`context_pressure_ratio` / `should_warn_context_pressure`,
  LP-0MSDCLQ2W001LGWC). Add a configurable compaction trigger ratio
  (default 0.70), distinct from the 0.8 diagnostic warn ratio (unchanged).
- **Compaction at prompt assembly:** session history is a message list;
  summarization/truncation operates on it before dispatch. Composes with
  slot save/restore (compacted prompts restore cleanly under the
  persistence cap).
- **Summarizer:** short proxy-generated summary (cheap local call) injected
  at the top of the prompt; with summarizer-unavailable fallback to the
  truncate backstop.
- **Logging:** every compaction event logs session, before/after estimated
  tokens, turns summarized, turns dropped, summary length — traceability
  for quality regressions (F3 §7). Nothing is silent.
- **Rollout phases:**
  1. **Warn-only dry-run** — advisory (would-summarize/would-drop) log +
     stats for 48h; validate churn (< 1 compaction/session/hour) against
     F1/F2 distributions; **no dispatch behavior change**.
  2. **Enforcement** — gated on the quality experiment (LP-0MSG9PUHU0059TTZ)
     passing its bar AND operator review of client-side compaction results.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1 Both modes: compacted prompt retains system prompt + very first user
  prompt verbatim + recent turns; middleware summarized (never silently
  dropped).
- AC2 Fast: est > 58,300 → compacted to ≤ 38K; backstop drop only for
  non-summarizable middle turns, logged, never system/first prompt.
- AC3 Cheap: est > 43,000 → compacted to ≤ 30K; non-compactable → remote
  with guidance (never silent remote, never near-full-slot local dispatch).
- AC4 Trigger routed through `context_pressure` machinery; compaction
  trigger ratio 0.70 configurable; 0.8 warn ratio behavior unchanged.
- AC5 All compaction events logged (session, before/after est tokens, turns
  summarized, turns dropped, summary length).
- AC6 Warn-only dry-run phase produces advisory logs + churn stats with
  zero dispatch changes; dry-run threshold validation recorded.
- AC7 Unit tests: retention invariant (first prompt kept), summary path,
  truncate backstop boundaries, turn-split prohibition, non-compactable
  routing, warn-only mode. Full suite green.
- AC8 Enforcement only after experiment (LP-0MSG9PUHU0059TTZ) passes its
  bar AND client-side compaction review (ContextHub WL-0MTBOXEGR009KDP6) is
  complete; no behavior change in warn-only phase.

## Interaction analysis (from F4 §5)

- **Slot save/restore:** summary + recent turns are byte-stable → clean
  restores under the persistence cap.
- **Hard-routing-cap companion (Tier 2, LP-0MTBOX45O005LD1S):** cap at
  70K/61.4K is the final bypass guard; compaction trigger fires below it so
  sessions rarely reach the cap.
- **KV-cache quantization (LP-0MSDCLQ2W001LGWC):** additive — compaction
  shrinks context length, q8_0 shrinks bytes/token; both raise decode
  headroom.

## Out of scope

- Client-side compaction UX (ContextHub owns it; see WL-0MTBOXEGR009KDP6).
- 150K–480K HTTP-400 cluster (LP-0MSC1BNP90017L9K).
- Changing the 0.8 diagnostic warn ratio.

## Dependencies

- Depends on LP-0MSG9PUHU0059TTZ (quality experiment) for the enforcement
  go/no-go.
- **Blocked pending:** client-side compaction results (ContextHub
  WL-0MTBOXEGR009KDP6 and completed compact-and-continue machinery) —
  operator decision 2026-08-28 to delay server-side until those are
  reviewed.
- Complementary to LP-0MTBOX45O005LD1S (Tier 2 hard cap + cheap gate).

## Objective

Execute the **24 h post-deploy verification of AC4** for `LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG`
(resident-prefix admission + session tenancy) on a restart-free production
window and record whether **scheduling-attributed** `prefill_deadline_exceeded`
cancellations fell by **≥ 90 %** against that same window's own re-anchored
baseline — plus the AC5 observability and AC6 lease-watchdog checks.

This item only measures and reports; it changes no scheduling logic.

## Problem statement

The epic's AC4 cannot be verified inside the implementing session: it needs a
full 24 h production soak on code that is actually running. Verification also
silently invalidates itself — the proxy restarted **six times on 2026-10-25**
(log rotations at 11:01:54, 11:21:20, 11:46:48, 18:57:27, 20:16:58 and
21:18:04 UTC), and each restart resets the in-memory residency/lease state, so
a window that contains a restart measures nothing. Without a pinned window,
attested uptime, and a window-scoped baseline, the ≥ 90 % claim is
unfalsifiable.

## Users

- **Proxy operator** — needs a defensible verdict on the thrash change before
  the epic closes, and needs to know whether to roll back.
  - *As the proxy operator, I want the 24 h result stated with its window,
    counts and baseline, so I can accept the change or roll it back.*
- **Implementing agents of the epic** — need AC4 satisfied by an independent
  measurement, not by their own in-session numbers.
  - *As the epic's implementing agent, I want the verdict recorded on the epic,
    so I can close AC4 without self-certifying.*
- **Future thrash investigations** — need the measured window, the corrected
  commands and the classifier rule as precedent.
  - *As a future investigator, I want the procedure and its numbers in
    `findings.md`, so I do not re-derive the methodology.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Preconditions attested before measuring.** The result records: the
  proxy PID and its start instant (`ps -o lstart -p <pid>`), continuous uptime
  covering the entire window, the code identity read **from the checkout the
  running proxy was started from** (`git log -1 --format=%H` — the checkout is
  shared, so the tip moves without a restart), and explicit confirmation that
  both target changes are in that tree (`LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG` ladder;
  `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D` 25k cold budget / 120 s deadline).
- **AC2 — Window pinned and restart-free.** The window is
  `2026-10-31T00:42:00Z → 2026-11-01T00:42:00Z` (ISO-8601 UTC, exactly 24 h,
  start ≥ the latest proxy restart; **re-arm #4**, after three restarts inside
  re-arm #3 — `2026-10-30T23:10:49Z`, `2026-10-31T00:37:53Z` and
  `2026-10-31T00:41:57Z` — invalidated it; see the re-arm #4 section at the top
  and comment `LP-C0MVWC0Y8C002ZWBT`). Re-arm trail: #1 `2026-10-25T21:19Z`,
  #2 `2026-10-27T10:17Z`, #3 `2026-10-30T10:36Z` — all invalidated by in-window
  restarts; #4 is current.
  Restart-freedom is evidenced by `ps -o lstart` plus the absence of
  `Logging initialised … pid=` / `Rotated previous proxy log aside` lines
  between start and end. A restart inside the window re-arms the run (new
  window, both windows recorded) and never yields a PASS.
- **AC3 — Absolute counts recorded.** `prefill_deadline_exceeded` events and
  total wasted prefill tokens for the window, with the
  `LP-0MVODJ3P6000AIUM` caveat stated (event fields are recomputed post-hoc, so
  `wasted_prefill_tokens` is overstated; the figure is either re-derived from
  admission-side data or reported with that caveat).
- **AC4 — Scheduling-attributed split, reproducible.** Every deadline event is
  classified as scheduling-attributed when either (a) the `reuse_ratio` logged
  at admission was below `server.local_resident_prefix_min_ratio`
  (0.5 in `proxy/config.yaml`), or (b) `slot_owner_session` at admission
  differs from the owner at the deadline event. Per-class counts are recorded;
  the remainder is reported as genuine GPU-speed misses and declared out of
  scope. Because the event line logs only `session` and `deadline`
  (`proxy/proxy/router.py` ~line 1616), the classifier joins each event to the
  session's most recent `routing_resident_prefix` line and any `local_eviction*`
  line before it — the join rule is stated in the result, and events whose
  join is ambiguous are counted separately and **not** as scheduling-attributed
  (conservative).
- **AC5 — Baseline re-anchored to the same window.** Baseline is computed by
  capturing the window with `capture_prefill_thrash_window.py` and replaying it
  through the residency ladder with `replay_prefill_occupancy.py
  --window-fixture`, and the reduction percentage against the
  scheduling-attributed count is stated explicitly. The 2026-10-24 figures
  (160 events / 5.4 h ≈ 780k wasted prefill tokens) are historical reference
  only and are never the baseline.
- **AC6 — Verdict recorded with both gates.** **PASS** requires (i) ≥ 90 %
  reduction in scheduling-attributed cancellations and (ii) no
  `local_lease_active` refusal window longer than the 180 s watchdog bound. On
  FAIL the measured numbers are recorded, a `discovered-from` item is created
  with the offending log extract, and this item is not marked complete.
- **AC7 — Staged-rollout observability check.** The window's
  `analyze_proxy_usage.py` report contains `## Residency-aware admission` with
  the `residency_decisions` / `residency_resident_admits` /
  `residency_evicted_denials` / `residency_tenant_limit_denials` /
  `local_evictions` counters and the per-session slot-owner churn table. An
  absent section, or decisions logged but all unmeasured, is a finding (ladder
  not emitting), never a pass.
- **AC8 — Result recorded and propagated.** One structured result comment on
  this item (window bounds, precondition attestation, counts, classified split,
  baseline, reduction %, verdict), cross-referenced from
  `LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG` and from
  `Post-deploy 24 h prefill regression verification (LP-0MVN4LD2F006B76I)`,
  which consumes the same report set (Q2 decision A) rather than running its
  own window.
- **AC9 — Documentation updated.** `docs/dev/slot-thrashing-investigation/findings.md`
  gains the measured window and verdict (and the corrected capture invocation
  with `--log`), so the 2026-10-24 numbers are labelled historical; all related
  documentation (code comments, README, docs site entries) is updated to
  reflect the changes.
- **AC10 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** (executed
  via the test skill / dev-push gate; no ad-hoc full-suite runs).

## Constraints

- **No restart inside the window.** Evidence that this is the dominant risk:
  six restarts on 2026-10-25 alone; the 21:18:10 restart was
  `source=manual actor=unknown`. A restart resets residency/lease state and
  invalidates the run.
- **Do not run before the pinned instant, and do not peek early** in a way that
  biases the decision.

## Summary

Measure whether the child-port discovery fix (LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF, deployed
2026-10-26T21:01Z) actually eliminates router-responder `GET /slots ... 500`
responses over a full 24 h production window, and record the raw counts as
auditable evidence.

**Earliest run: 2026-10-27T12:00Z.** Window:
**2026-10-27T12:00Z → 2026-10-28T12:00Z.** If the fix (or a follow-up restart)
lands later than that, shift the window to start 24 h after the last relevant
deployment and record the new timestamps in a comment.

**Window state verified at planning (2026-10-28T04:40Z):** the window is
**still open** (≈7 h 20 m remaining at verification time). Production facts:
proxy pid **3791954** started **2026-10-27T10:16:11Z** and is still running
(18 h 23 m uptime) — the fixed proxy has been up continuously since **before**
the window opened, and **no proxy restart has occurred inside the window**, so
the AC6 restart condition is satisfiable. No pre-window baseline comment was
recorded at 12:00Z; see "Baseline reconstruction" under the execute-time plan
for why the counter delta is nonetheless provable.

## Problem statement

Router-proxied `GET /slots` polls returned HTTP 500 at ~9 % during giant
prefills because child-port discovery silently failed and every proxy poll
traversed the router. The fix replaced discovery with a rotation-proof signal
and routed every call site through it, but the only proof that matters is a
production 24 h window with zero such 500s — the pre-fix evidence (1,754
router 500s in the 2026-10-26 log) is not proof of absence.

## Users

- **Producer / maintainer** — "As the operator, I want a dated, reproducible
  measurement of router-responder `/slots` 500s so I can close the residual-500
  bug and trust the fix, instead of re-reading raw logs myself."
- **On-call agent (herdr downtime worker)** — "As an unattended agent, I want a
  deterministic method and explicit verdict rule so my pass/fail report does
  not depend on my own judgement of ambiguous counts."
- **Downstream users** — chat/agent clients that see 500s and 5–7 s slot-poll
  latency when slot queries serialise behind a busy child.

## Acceptance Criteria

Refined at intake per producer decisions Q1(a), Q2(b), Q3(a):

- **AC1** — **Chat-model path: zero.** The windowed count of router-responder
  `GET /slots ... 500` responses attributable to the chat model is **0**.
  Responder split: lines with no `[pid]` prefix are the router, `[pid]`-prefixed
  lines are the model children; per-file counts are reported for every
  `llama-server*.log` file whose mtime falls inside the window (Q1a).
- **AC2** — **Raw router and child counts reported**, so a silent switch back to
  router polling cannot masquerade as a pass: router-responder `GET /slots`
  200 / 400 / 500 and model-child 200 / 400 / 500 counts for each file in the
  window. `scripts/slots_500_triage.py` output is attached verbatim.
- **AC3** — **`slots_stale` share reported** for `status_request` polls in the
  window: the primary figure is *all* `status_request` polls (directly
  comparable to the pre-fix baseline **579/899** in the 2026-10-26 file), with
  the active-prefill subset (`active_query=true` or `local_active_query=true`)
  reported as a secondary figure (Q3a).
- **AC4** — **Fallback evidence reported, split by path** (Q2b):
  `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"}`
  delta across the window plus the (throttled, undercounting)
  `slots_child_port_unavailable` warning lines, attributed by model.
  - Chat-model (`Qwen3`) fallbacks: **any occurrence fails the check.**
  - Embed-model (`mxbai-embed`) fallbacks: reported separately as a
    **non-blocking observation**; if any occur, a new bug item is filed at
    window end, linked `discovered-from:LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF`.
- **AC5** — **Reproducibility:** the exact commands/regexes (or script
  invocations) used, the window start/end timestamps, the pre-window baseline
  snapshot (counter values, log line count, proxy pid + start time) and the raw
  counts are all recorded as a work-item comment.
- **AC6** — **Restart integrity:** any proxy restart inside the window is
  detected (pid change) and reported; if one occurred, the counter delta is
  declared unavailable and the verdict relies on per-file log counts with the
  limitation stated explicitly.
- **AC7** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC8** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Method (agreed: Q1 option (a) — hybrid)

Measured with existing tooling plus two log families:

```bash
# 1. Window-start snapshot (also record: date -u, pid start time, log line count)
date -u; ps -o lstart= -p "$(pgrep -f 'uvicorn proxy.server:app')"
wc -l < /var/log/llama-proxy/llama-server.log
curl -s localhost:8000/metrics | grep 'llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total'

# 2. Window-end snapshot (same commands, 24 h later) -> counter delta = exact
#    windowed fallbacks when the proxy was not restarted in between.

# 3. Responder/status split per file (reuses the triage CLI: no timestamps in
#    llama-server logs, so scope by the files whose mtime falls in the window)
python3 scripts/slots_500_triage.py --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy --llama-file 'llama-server.log' --summary

# 4. Fallback warnings (throttled to one line per interval -> undercounts;
#    the counter above is authoritative)
grep -c 'slots_child_port_unavailable' /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log

# slots_stale share (existing baseline method)
grep -o 'slots_stale=[a-z]*' /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log | sort | uniq -c
```

Take a **pre-window baseline snapshot** immediately before
2026-10-27T12:00Z (counter values + `llama-server.log` line count + proxy pid
start time) so the window delta is unambiguous.

> **Status: not done.** No snapshot comment exists for 2026-10-27T12:00Z. The
execution plan below reconstructs the baseline from monotonic-counter
evolution plus pid `lstart`, and states the limitation explicitly (AC5).

## Execution plan (exact recipe — run at/after 2026-10-28T12:00Z)

Steps 0–2 must be re-verified at run time, not trusted from this block; they
are read-only and cheap. Steps 3–6 produce the evidence; step 7 records it.

### Step 0 — window gate

Do **not** measure before **2026-10-28T12:00Z**. An earlier run measures a
partial window and is not acceptable as the AC evidence.

### Step 1 — restart integrity (AC6)

```bash
date -u
ps -o pid,lstart,etime -p "$(pgrep -f 'uvicorn proxy.server:app' | head -1)"
```

Expected: a single pid **3791954** with `lstart` **2026-10-27T10:16:11Z** ⇒ no
restart inside the window. Any other pid/`lstart` ⇒ record the restart time,
declare the counter delta unavailable, and fall back to per-file log counts
with the limitation stated (AC6).

### Step 2 — fallback counter (AC4, exact)

```bash
curl -s localhost:8000/metrics | grep 'llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total'
```

A Prometheus counter that has never been incremented emits **no sample line**
(only `# HELP` / `# TYPE`). That is the state observed at planning — quote the
raw output verbatim, because "absent sample" is the auditable form of "0".
Range-vector deltas are not needed: a monotonic counter reading 0 on a process
that started before the window ⇒ windowed delta = 0.

### Baseline reconstruction (AC5, replaces the missed 12:00Z snapshot)

State the limitation explicitly and rebuild the baseline from: proxy pid +
`lstart` (step 1); the counter's never-incremented state (step 2); the per-file
line counts read at window end. The proof is monotonicity, not a start sample:
the process started 1 h 44 m before the window opened and its counter is still
0.

### Step 3 — llama-server file set (AC1 / AC2)

```bash
ls -l --time-style=full-iso /var/log/llama-proxy/llama-server*.log*
```

Window set (mtime inside 2026-10-27T12:00Z → 2026-10-28T12:00Z):
`llama-server.log-2026-10-28` (logrotate `copytruncate` copy at 00:00Z; content
= 2026-10-27T00:00Z → 2026-10-28T00:00Z) and the live `llama-server.log`
(content = 2026-10-28T00:00Z → window end). `llama-server.log-2026-10-27.gz`
has mtime 2026-10-27T00:00Z ⇒ outside the window, exclude it.

llama-server access lines carry **no timestamps**, so this union covers
2026-10-27T00:00Z → window end: a **superset** of the window, carrying 12 h of
extra pre-window traffic. Consequence: **zero router-responder 500s across the
superset proves zero inside the window** (report the over-count direction); a
non-zero count needs the per-file split plus the caveat that the window
boundary is approximate at ±12 h granularity.


`copytruncate` copy (`proxy.log-YYYY-MM-DD_HH`) can duplicate a range — so
**file names do not reliably delimit the window**. Derive each candidate's own
first/last timestamp from its lines, keep the parts intersecting the window,
and dedupe overlapping ranges (keep one generation per timestamp range):


One comment recording: window start/end; `date -u` at run time; pid + `lstart`

the `proxy.log` file set with each file's observed first/last timestamp; the

## Goal

As an operator I need a **measured, reproducible verdict** on whether
`/sys/class/drm/card0/device/gpu_metrics` (the `amd_gpu_metrics_v3_0` blob, the
interface `amdgpu_top` reads) carries a *graded* GFX-activity signal on this
Strix Halo APU — one that separates compute from idle the way the
power-derived `gpu:computing:bool` rule does but `gpu_busy_percent` does not —
and, only if such a field passes an explicit discrimination bar, to have it
published as a Prometheus series through the existing 10 s textfile sampler.
A negative verdict, recorded with numbers so the path is never retried, is an
equally valid outcome.

## Problem statement

The usage report's GPU busy time infers activity from power draw
(`gpu:computing:bool >= bool 90`), which cannot tell GFX work from any other
power draw. `gpu_busy_percent` was eliminated as a utilisation signal
(2026-10-28: 45.2 % false-busy, Pearson r = 0.28 against power,
LP-0MVSQQO910077LYL), leaving `gpu_metrics` as the last candidate hardware
activity source. **Intake measurements (2026-10-29) show that candidate is very
probably dead too**: `average_gfx_activity` read **100 % on every one of 120
samples across two captures** while package power moved between 42 W and 123 W
and DRAM bandwidth between 0.7 and 59.5 GB/s. This item therefore exists to
settle the question with evidence and a stated bar, not to assume the answer.

## Users

- **Operator (primary).** "Is the GPU actually doing work right now, and was it
  busy between 17:00 and 19:00?" — needs a utilisation figure that is a direct
  measurement, not a power-draw proxy.
- **Agent answering a usage/incident question (secondary).** Needs to know which
  hardware fields are trustworthy on this host so it cites a real signal instead
  of re-litigating `gpu_busy_percent`.

User stories:

- As an operator I can run one command that decodes `gpu_metrics`, samples it
  alongside power and `gpu_busy_percent`, and prints per-field discrimination
  statistics — so the verdict rests on numbers I can reproduce.
- As an operator I am told plainly whether the interface gives a graded signal,
  with the capture date, kernel, sample counts and band means, so I never
  re-investigate it.
- As an operator, if a field does pass, the series appears next to the existing
  `gpu_*` textfile series without a new daemon, port or scrape job.

## Existing state (measured during intake, 2026-10-29, kernel 7.0.0-34-generic)

| Question | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Is the file live and readable? | `-r--r--r-- 4096` root:root; 264 bytes of content; values change between reads; no root, no ROCm, no `amd-smi` needed |
| Which structure? | Header decodes to `structure_size=264, format_revision=3, content_revision=0` → `struct gpu_metrics_v3_0` (`drivers/gpu/drm/amd/include/kgd_pp_interface.h`; the same header text is vendored in `libdrm_amdgpu_sys`'s `wrapper_gpu_metrics.h`) |
| Does the layout check out? | Field sizes under `#pragma pack(4)` sum to 260 B; 4 B tail padding = **264 B**, matching `structure_size` exactly. Cross-checks: `average_socket_power` 95 060 mW vs hwmon `power1_average` 95.06 W (0.1 % agreement); `average_gfx_power` 11.3–44.2 W; `average_gfxclk_frequency` 2 711–2 900 MHz; `average_dram_reads` 0.7–59.5 GB/s; `average_vcn_activity` 0; `average_ipu_activity` all 0; `temperature_gfx` 56–69 °C |
| Does the activity field discriminate? | **No.** Capture A (60 samples @1 s): power 44–123 W, DRAM 1.8–59.5 GB/s → `average_gfx_activity` = 100 on all 60. Capture B (60 samples @1 s): power 42–66 W (idle band), DRAM 0.7–3.5 GB/s → 100 on all 60. Spot samples earlier: 97, 99, 100 at 41–57 W |
| How does it compare with the rejected counter? | Identically saturated: `gpu_busy_percent` = 100 on all 120 samples of both captures; `rocm-smi --showuse` reports `GPU use 100 %` at 54 W. GFX clock is pinned at its 2 900 MHz maximum in *both* bands, so the GFX domain is never gated while the proxy holds the device |
| What *does* vary with load? | `average_dram_reads`/`average_dram_writes` (memory bandwidth, 0.7 → 59.5 GB/s), `average_gfx_power` (11.3 → 44.2 W), `average_socket_power` (42 → 123 W), `average_core_c0_activity` (per-core C0 residency) |
| Are the values instantaneous? | No — they are SMU **time filtered** (`time_filter_alphavalue` = 1 000 000); the filter window is undocumented, so no claim finer than the sample interval is supportable |

Existing pipeline this would plug into: `gpu-metrics.service` runs
`~/.local/bin/gpu-metrics-textfile.sh` every 10 s, writing `gpu.prom` into
node_exporter's textfile collector (`gpu_busy_percent`, `gpu_vram_*`,
`gpu_gtt_used_bytes`, label `gpu="card0"`), scraped every 15 s by Prometheus;
documented in [docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service](../../docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service)
and [monitoring/README.md](../../monitoring/README.md).

## Desired change

1. **A reproducible probe CLI** — `scripts/gpu_metrics_probe.py`: decode the
   v3.0 blob from a sysfs path (default
   `/sys/class/drm/card0/device/gpu_metrics`), sample every candidate activity
   field alongside the two reference signals (amdgpu hwmon `power1_average` and
   `gpu_busy_percent`) at a configurable interval for a configurable duration,
   and emit CSV or `--json`. A `--verdict` mode prints the per-field
   discrimination statistics against the bar below.
2. **A recorded verdict** — the measured numbers plus a pass/fail decision per
   candidate field, written into the work item and the two monitoring documents,
   so the interface is either adopted once or closed off permanently.
3. **Conditional publication** — only if a field passes the bar, publish it
   through the existing 10 s textfile sampler (new `# HELP`/`# TYPE` series with
   the `gpu="card0"` label, atomic write, nothing written on read failure). If
   nothing passes, publish nothing and record why.
4. **A regression guard** — a saturated activity field must not be usable as a
   utilisation input in any rule or report query without a test failing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `scripts/gpu_metrics_probe.py` decodes `gpu_metrics` into named fields
  using the pinned v3.0 layout and validates the header
  (`structure_size` == layout size, `format_revision` == 3); unit tests cover a
  real 264-byte capture committed as a fixture, a truncated buffer, and an
  unknown `format_revision`/`structure_size`, which must be rejected with a
  clear error rather than misparsed.
- [ ] A capture (`--duration`/`--interval`, defaults documented) writes one row
  per sample containing a timestamp, every candidate activity field,
  `power1_average_watts` and `gpu_busy_percent`; a test drives the sampler
  against fixture sysfs trees (fake `/sys/class/drm/card0/device` and hwmon
  directory) and asserts row count, monotonic timestamps and fixture-derived
  values, without sleeping.
- [ ] `--verdict` reports, per candidate field, the idle-band mean (< 60 W), the
  compute-band mean (≥ 90 W), their separation in percentage points, Pearson r
  against package power, and the idle-band false-busy share (samples ≥ 90 %
  while power < 60 W); a field passes only if separation ≥ 30 pp **and**
  r ≥ 0.6 **and** idle-band false-busy ≤ 10 %. Unit tests drive synthetic
  saturated, graded and noisy series and assert the exact pass/fail decision and
  the printed statistics.
- [ ] The measured numbers and the resulting verdict — positive **or** negative
  — are recorded in `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service`,
  `monitoring/README.md` (the "Why not `amd-smi`, `rocm-smi` or `amdtop`?"
  section gains a `gpu_metrics` row) and the work item, including capture date,
  kernel version, sample counts and band statistics; a negative verdict is a
  complete outcome, not a failure.
- [ ] If a field passed, the 10 s textfile sampler publishes it (series name,
  `# HELP`/`# TYPE`, `gpu="card0"` label) with the existing atomic-write and
  write-nothing-on-failure behaviour, and `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service`
  documents the series and its meaning; a test runs the sampler against fixture
  sysfs and asserts its emitted series set exactly matches the set the
  documentation table lists (so docs and behaviour cannot drift). If no field
  passed, no new series is added and the test asserts the sampler's series set is
  unchanged.
- [ ] The pinned-counter guard in `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py`
  (`FORBIDDEN_RULE_SERIES`) is extended so a saturated activity field cannot
  appear as a utilisation input — `gpu_busy_percent` always, and the
  `gpu_metrics` activity fields when the verdict is negative — with a regression
  test that fails if any `monitoring/*.yaml` rule expression or the probe's own
  utilisation expressions select one.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, docstrings, `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service` and
  `monitoring/README.md`; the probe's re-measure procedure (how to re-run the
  capture after a kernel, firmware or driver change) is documented.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes via `/skill:test`.

## Constraints

- **No new daemon, port or scrape job.** Reuse `gpu-metrics.service` →
  node_exporter textfile collector; the sampler's 10 s cadence and Prometheus's
  15 s scrape interval are the resolution floor and must be stated as such.
- **Host state is part of the deliverable.** The sampler script lives in
  `~/.local/bin/gpu-metrics-textfile.sh` and is documented in
  `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service`; any change to its series must be reflected
  there so a clean clone can reproduce it.
- **Repository boundary.** `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/` (`gpu_busy.py`,
  `reporting.py`) is not edited — adopting a passing field in the daily report is
  a follow-up item, mirroring the constraint recorded in LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W.
- **The layout must be pinned in-repo.** The struct is not shipped in the
  installed `linux-headers` packages on this host, so the field table must be
  transcribed with a cited source (`struct gpu_metrics_v3_0`) and validated
  against the observed 264-byte `structure_size`; it must fail closed when the
  kernel reports a different revision.
- **No instantaneous claims.** The values are SMU time-filtered with an
  undocumented window; the output must say so rather than imply per-second
  fidelity.
- **Read cost.** One 264-byte sysfs read per sample; world-readable, no root, no
  ROCm userspace, no `amd-smi`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/gpu_metrics_probe.py` — New. v3.0 decoder (field table + header
  validation), paired sampler for `gpu_metrics` + hwmon power + `gpu_busy_percent`,
  band statistics and the pass/fail verdict; CSV and `--json` output.
- `tests/test_gpu_metrics_probe.py` — New. Decoder fixtures (real 264-byte
  capture, truncated, unknown revision), fixture-sysfs sampling, verdict
  arithmetic and boundary cases (power exactly 60 W / 90 W, activity exactly
  90 %).
- `tests/fixtures/gpu_metrics_v3_0.bin` — New. One committed real capture so the
  layout assertion is reproducible.
- `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service` — Record the verdict, the decode layout and
  (conditionally) the new series; extend the verification section with the probe
  command.
- `monitoring/README.md` — Add `gpu_metrics` to "Why not `amd-smi`, `rocm-smi`
  or `amdtop`?" with the measured band statistics; note the re-measure recipe.
- `monitoring/gpu_compute_rules.yaml` — Header comment records the `gpu_metrics`
  verdict (no rule change expected; the power rule stays authoritative).
- `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py` — Extend `FORBIDDEN_RULE_SERIES`
  so saturated activity fields are rejected as utilisation inputs.
- `~/.local/bin/gpu-metrics-textfile.sh` — Only if a field passed: emit the new
  series from the same atomic write.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: the premise is false.** Intake evidence already shows
  `average_gfx_activity` saturated at 100 % from 42 W to 123 W. Mitigation: the
  negative verdict is an explicit, accepted outcome (AC4) and the probe records
  which fields *do* discriminate (DRAM bandwidth, GFX power) for a follow-up.
- **Risk: decoder drift after a kernel or firmware upgrade.** Mitigation: header
  validation plus a committed real capture; the probe refuses unknown revisions
  and the docs carry the re-measure procedure.
- **Risk: undocumented APU field semantics.** `average_gfx_activity` may mean
  "GFX domain powered" rather than "GFX busy" on SMU 14. Mitigation: the bar and
  band statistics decide it, and the interpretation limits are documented.
- **Risk: a capture that misses one band.** A verdict computed only from idle
  samples would be meaningless. Mitigation: AC3 requires both bands, and the
  probe reports per-band sample counts so a one-sided capture is visible.
- **Risk: scope creep** into report integration, new daemons or a full GPU
  telemetry redesign. Mitigation: those are explicit constraints/follow-ups, not
  scope.
- **Assumption:** amdgpu hwmon `power1_average` remains the reference compute
  signal (idle ≈ 40–54 W, computing ≈ 115 W, threshold 90 W) per
  LP-0MVO8DOHP008FL48; this item does not re-derive the threshold.
- **Assumption:** the discrimination bar (≥ 30 pp separation, r ≥ 0.6, ≤ 10 %
  idle false-busy) is strict enough — it is far stricter than
  `gpu_busy_percent`'s measured 45.2 % false-busy — and is recorded here so the
  producer can tighten or relax it before implementation.
- **Assumption:** both bands occur on this host within a short window (intake saw
  idle at 42–66 W and compute at 90–123 W within ~15 minutes), so a 30-minute
  capture is sufficient; longer captures are supported by the same CLI.
- **Assumption:** priority stays `high` — the verdict decides whether a direct
  hardware utilisation measure is possible at all on this host, which the usage
  report's honesty goal depends on — even though the likely outcome is a short
  negative report rather than a code change.

**Discovered while producing the AC4 post-change record** (`LP-0MVTKTOVI006ZONN`; record: `docs/dev/prefill-admission-conversion-postchange.md`). **Not a release blocker**: the literal parent AC4 bar (< 85 %) and the no-new-eviction clause both hold. This item tracks the *stricter* working-baseline regression that the same record reports.

## Finding (committed harness, same 24 h basis, same code path per window)

Post-change window `2026-10-29 00:10:18` → `2026-10-30 00:10:18` UTC (deploy `52085f09`) vs pre-change `2026-10-27 19:00` → `2026-10-28 19:00`.

- Abandoned-queue-wait share: **36.9 % (24/65) → 60.7 % (314/517)**.
- Abandoned waits per hour: **1.0 /h → 13.1 /h**; queued local waits per hour **2.7 /h → 21.5 /h**.
- Admits/hour **17.6 → 53.3** (×3.0), rejects/hour **164.8 → 114.3** (×0.69) — the queue denominator grew with traffic, but the *share* also grew in four of five bands (`<8k` 35.1→49.5, `8k-20k` 50.0→64.6, `20k-32k` 0→78.8, `32k-64k` 0→91.1).
- Evictions are **not** the cause: `local_eviction_after_acceptance` 392 (16.3 /h) vs 463 (19.3 /h) pre-change, all five reason classes pre-existing.

## Goal (user story)

As the LLM proxy operator I want to understand why the abandoned-queue-wait share rose after the contended-pricing fix — despite the contended bucket and the occupant-remaining rebase provably serving — so that queue-budget/ETA behaviour under the new (~3×) local admission volume is correct rather than merely below the historical 85 % bar.

## Open questions for intake

- Is the rise a *fundamental* consequence of admitting ~3× more local dispatches (more marginal admits queue, then hit the 60 s `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` budget), i.e. the admission guard is now too **permissive** rather than too optimistic?
- Why does band `32k-64k` show 45 queued waits and 41 abandoned (91.1 %) with **zero** admits — where do those queued waits come from if every admission in that band was rejected?
- Should the working baseline be recomputed on a diurnally matched window (`00:10`→`00:10` pre-change) before calling this a regression? Both windows are exactly 24 h, so per-hour rates are comparable, but the mix is not identical.

## Evidence

- `docs/dev/prefill-admission-conversion-postchange.md` / `.json` (source numbers; reproducible)
- `scripts/prefill_admission_conversion.py --since "2026-10-29 00:10:18" --until "2026-10-30 00:10:18" --json` (eviction counters included)
- Parent epic: `LP-0MVS8T6F4006DGG3`; AC4 record carrier: `LP-0MVTKTOVI006ZONN`


## Measured refinement (planning session, 2026-10-30)

The three intake questions are answered below with numbers reproducible from
`/var/log/llama-proxy` using the committed harness vocabulary. Two of the
answers change the framing of this item before any behaviour change is
planned.

### 1. The baseline window is diurnally mismatched — most of the headline is mix

The fix was deployed at `2026-10-29 00:10:18` UTC (`52085f09`), so
`2026-10-28 00:10:18` → `2026-10-29 00:10:18` UTC is a **fully pre-change-code**
24 h window that is diurnally matched to the post-change window:

| Window (24 h) | Code | Enqueued waits | Abandoned | Share | Admits | Rejects |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `10-27 19:00` → `10-28 19:00` | pre | 65 | 24 | 36.9 % | 423 | 3 954 |
| `10-28 00:10:18` → `10-29 00:10:18` | pre | 136 | 71 | **52.6 %** | 576 | 4 078 |
| `10-29 00:10:18` → `10-30 00:10:18` | `52085f09` | 517 | 314 | 60.7 % | 1 278 | 2 742 |

So the like-for-like change is **52.6 % → 60.7 % (+8.1 points)**; the
36.9 % → 52.6 % step is diurnal mix (the 19:00→19:00 window is quieter), not
the contended-pricing change. This answers open question 3: yes, the baseline
must be recomputed diurnally, and it is a measurement slice of its own
(`LP-0MVV29XDW006VTWK`).

### 2. Per-band numbers are contaminated by a harness attribution defect

`build_report()`'s `band_for_queue()` bands a queue wait by the session's
nearest *preceding* admission and, when none precedes, falls back to
`(preceding or candidates)[-1:]` — the session's latest admission, **even one
hours after the queue event**. That is the origin of the phantom `32k-64k` row
(45 queued waits / 41 abandoned / **0 admits**): those waits belong to sessions
whose only admission evidence is a later `prefill_budget_exceeded` reject.
Verified example: session `herdr-1793285755-177798-1619` abandons at
`14:56:57` and its only admission line is a 35 077-token reject at `15:01:35`
(4 m 38 s later). The **totals are unaffected** (banding does not change them),
but every per-band claim — including "the share grew in four of five bands" —
is untrustworthy until fixed (`LP-0MVV29WR0009DY1A`). This answers open
question 2: those waits are an attribution artefact, to be proven per-wait by
`LP-0MVV29XPT003OXI5`.

### 3. Every abandonment is a budget expiry, not a depth refusal

`queued_duration >= 55 s` for **314/314** post-change and **71/71** pre-change
diurnal abandonments; depth-cap refusals (`elapsed ≈ 0`) do not occur. The 60 s
`contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` budget is the binding constraint, not
`contention_queue_max_depth` (8). Today that distinction is inferred from the
duration rather than logged (`LP-0MVV29X2E004INFL`).

### 4. Two entry paths, one of them a retry without priority

| Window (24 h) | lease-active waits / abandoned | concurrency-limit waits / abandoned |
|---|---|---|
| `10-27 19:00` → `10-28 19:00` | 48 / 20 = 41.7 % | 17 / 4 = 23.5 % |
| `10-28 00:10:18` → `10-29 00:10:18` | 107 / 57 = 53.3 % | 28 / 14 = 50.0 % |
| `10-29 00:10:18` → `10-30 00:10:18` | 368 / 225 = 61.1 % | 149 / 89 = 59.7 % |

225 of 314 post-change abandonments (71.7 %) carry `reason=local_lease_active`:
the local dispatch already returned a `local_lease_active` 503 and the request
re-entered `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot` to wait for the protected slot. That
call site passes **no `priority=`**, so the documented "high priority never
queues" contract is not enforced there, and a request that already spent its
queue budget can be handed a fresh 60 s (`LP-0MVV29Y1M004GAW0`).

### 5. The guard admits waits it cannot serve — leading cause hypothesis

For 176 of the 314 abandoned waits a preceding `local_admission_guard`
decision exists in the same session: **170 are `admit`**, median
`projected_wait_s = 35.8 s` (75 of them < 30 s) against an observed 60 s wait.
(Session-level join; own-request correlation is a deliverable of
`LP-0MVV29XPT003OXI5`.) The guard prices peer *prefill* service — including the
re-priced occupant remaining new tokens — but not the time a lease holder keeps
the slot while **generating**. This answers open question 1: the shape is a
slot-release modelling gap more than ETA "permissiveness", and it must be
confirmed per-wait before any behaviour change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The abandoned-queue-wait share is restated on a diurnally matched basis (both windows `00:10:18`→`00:10:18` UTC, 24 h, pre-change code ending exactly at the `52085f09` deploy) measured with the same harness revision as the post-change window, and the diurnal-mix contribution is separated from the code-change contribution in a committed record.
- AC2: Queue-wait band attribution is defect-free: no wait is banded by an admission belonging to a different (later or stale) request, a wait with no own-request evidence is reported as `unknown`, and the phantom band (queued waits with zero admission verdicts) is resolved. Unit-tested from synthetic log lines.
- AC3: Queue waits are attributable by entry path (`trigger=concurrency_limit|local_lease_active`) and abandon cause (`cause=queue_wait_expired|queue_depth_exceeded`), logged rather than inferred from duration, reported per trigger/cause, and unit-tested including the pre-change log shape (missing fields degrade to `unknown`).
- AC4: A committed diagnosis record states the cause of the residual (diurnally matched) rise with per-wait evidence: the same-request guard projection vs the observed wait, and the blocker class (prefill in flight vs lease holder generating) that held the slot — explicitly answering whether the guard is too permissive in the ETA sense or blind to the blocker's slot-release time.
- AC5: The `local_lease_active` re-queue path honours the request's priority (`high` never queues there) and charges one queue budget per turn, so cumulative queue wait for a turn cannot exceed `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`; asserted by unit tests.
- AC6: The diagnosed blocker class is priced in the admission guard (or a committed decision records the measured rationale for no change): the guard never admits a queue wait that cannot be served inside the remaining budget because the blocker keeps the slot after its prefill. Rollback uses existing knobs only, the symmetric `eta * busy_slots` floor is never lowered, fail-open is preserved, `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` (60) / `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` (120) are unchanged, the `60 < 120 < 840 < 900` ordering test stays green, and lease-fairness capping remains owned by `LP-0MVOJ6KAW004EBV0`.
- AC7: A post-fix 24 h window is measured with the same harness and committed; the abandoned share, per-trigger/cause shares and `local_eviction_after_acceptance` classes are compared against the diurnally matched baseline and the literal 85 % bar, with per-hour rates alongside shares.
- AC8: Full test suite green at the pushed commit, and the operator docs (`docs/dev/contended-prefill-pricing.md`, the pre/post-change records) carry the restated baseline and the post-fix verdict.

## Plan

Test-first, dependency-ordered slices (each is a vertical slice: code + tests +
docs/record where it applies). Blocked-by edges are wired in Worklog; the
implementing session must run them in this order.

| # | Work item | Scope | Blocked by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `LP-0MVV29WR0009DY1A` | Fix queue-wait band attribution in the conversion harness (own-request join + carry `new_tokens` on the queue lines; no phantom bands) | — |
| 2 | `LP-0MVV29X2E004INFL` | Attribute queue waits by entry path (`trigger=`) and abandon cause (`cause=`), logged not inferred; harness reports the split | 1 |
| 3 | `LP-0MVV29XDW006VTWK` | Restate the baseline on the diurnally matched 24 h window (52.6 % vs 60.7 %) as a committed record | 1, 2 |
| 4 | `LP-0MVV29XPT003OXI5` | Per-wait diagnosis: same-request guard projection vs observed wait, blocker class, phantom-band proof, +8.1-point attribution | 3 |
| 5 | `LP-0MVV29Y1M004GAW0` | Fix the lease-active re-queue path: pass `priority=`, one queue budget per turn | 2 |
| 6 | `LP-0MVV29YDQ00437N6` | Price the diagnosed blocker class in the guard (or record a no-change decision); no new knob, guardrails unchanged | 4, 5 |
| 7 | `LP-0MVV29YP6006PLNP` | Re-measure the 24 h post-fix share against the diurnal baseline + 85 % bar; update docs/records (runnable deploy+24 h) | 6 |

**Assumptions recorded (see Appendix comment).** (a) The diurnally matched
window is the fair working baseline; the 36.9 % 19:00→19:00 figure is retained
as a historical reference and the parent epic's literal 85 % bar is unchanged.
(b) The 60.7 % total share is taken as correct for the post-change window
(banding does not affect totals) while per-band numbers are treated as
provisional until slice 1 lands. (c) No behaviour change is made before slice 4
produces evidence; slice 6 may legitimately close as a documented no-change
decision. (d) Slice 7 is time-gated on the slice-6 deploy and must stand down
if started early.

## Goal (user story)

As the LLM proxy operator, I want every queued local wait to record *how it
entered the queue* and *why it left without a slot*, so the abandoned-wait
share can be split by entry path and by cause instead of being a single
opaque 60.7 % — and so a full-budget expiry can never be confused with a
depth-cap refusal.

## Measured need (parent LP-0MVV1V213002QAIR)

Two entry paths feed one queue, and only one of them logs a reason:

| Path | Call site | Abandonments (post-change 24 h) | Logged reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| `local_concurrency_limit` | `provider.py` first `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot` call | 89 / 314 (28.3 %) | **none** (the fallback line has no `reason=` field there) |
| `local_lease_active` retry | `provider.py` second `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot` call, after the local dispatch returned a `local_lease_active` 503 | 225 / 314 (71.7 %) | `reason=local_lease_active` |

Per-window split already derivable from the existing `reason=` field (own
measurement, same harness vocabulary):

| Window (24 h) | Enqueued | Abandoned | Share | lease-active share | concurrency-limit share |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `2026-10-27 19:00` → `10-28 19:00` (pre) | 65 | 24 | 36.9 % | 41.7 % (20/48) | 23.5 % (4/17) |
| `2026-10-28 00:10:18` → `10-29 00:10:18` (pre, diurnal) | 136 | 71 | 52.6 % | 53.3 % (57/107) | 50.0 % (14/28) |
| `2026-10-29 00:10:18` → `10-30 00:10:18` (`52085f09`) | 517 | 314 | 60.7 % | 61.1 % (225/368) | 59.7 % (89/149) |

Also measured: **all** abandonments are full-budget expiries
(`queued_duration >= 55 s`; 314/314 post-change, 71/71 pre-change diurnal);
depth-cap refusals (`elapsed ≈ 0`) do not occur, so the 60 s
`contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` budget is the binding constraint, not
`contention_queue_max_depth`. That distinction is currently *inferred* from
the duration rather than logged.

## Scope

- Log `trigger=concurrency_limit|local_lease_active` on both queue outcomes
  and on the enqueue line, and an explicit `cause=queue_wait_expired|
  queue_depth_exceeded` on both fallback call sites.

Same-window trend of the metric on successive builds:

|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-24 20:00 → 07:00 (night) | `56a3a28a`/`2d2b6b51` (router `/slots` path) | 79.61 % |

but **77 % of the residual stale polls were served from cache after a refresh that took longer than
the 2 s counts / 1.0 s (`STATUS_QUERY_TIMEOUT`) detail budget**. Staleness is therefore no longer a
router artefact: the `/slots` read path still exceeds its budget under load, so `slots_stale` is
reporting real latency, not a truthfulness defect (the cache-time reconciliation of

# finish pushes from the main checkout after a refused local-dev fast-forward, so the pushed-commit guard refuses

**Discovered during:** LP-0MVU7ZYWS002RDYM (guard test: no proxy `/slots` without `?model=`) on 2026-10-31.

## Summary

When `implement.py finish` cannot fast-forward the main checkout's local `dev` to the new commit (because a concurrent session moved `dev` since the worktree was created), it logs the refusal, then pushes anyway — **from the main checkout**, whose `HEAD` is therefore still the pre-existing `dev` tip. The repo's `pre-push` pushed-commit guard (LP-0MVSJUM3O003C0H9, `.githooks/pre-push` §3a) correctly refuses, because the tree it would measure is not the pushed commit. `finish`'s own rebase-and-retry then produces a fresh commit that is a proper descendant of `origin/dev`, but it still pushes from the main checkout, so the guard refuses again and the item is left `open` with the work committed only on the feature branch.

## Observed sequence (2026-10-31, LP-0MVU7ZYWS002RDYM)

1. Worktree branched from `dev` = `a3f09939`. While working, another item pushed `50167e00`; main checkout local `dev` = `50167e00`.
2. `finish` committed `b2ec8b55` (parent `a3f09939`) in the worktree.
3. Fast-forward of main `dev` → refused: `b2ec8b55` is not a descendant of `origin/dev` (`50167e00`). (Correct — but it must not fall through to a push that the guard will refuse.)
4. `finish` rebased the branch onto `50167e00` → `bb326ecf` (now a proper descendant of `origin/dev`).
5. Push ran with cwd = **main checkout** (`git_push_to_dev(repo_root, ...)`), refspec `<branch>:refs/heads/dev`.
6. Guard refused: `pushed commit (refs/heads/dev): bb326ecf`, `checked-out HEAD: 50167e00`, `gate tree: /home/rgardler/projects/llm`.
7. Recovery was a manual `git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/dev` **from the worktree** (clean, checked out at `bb326ecf`), which is the hook's own documented alternative — the full-suite gate then measured the correct tree.

## Why it matters

The refusal loop is unrecoverable from inside `finish`: every retry re-commits/re-pushes from the same wrong cwd, so a routine concurrent push turns into a manual recovery step, and concurrent sessions wedge each other. It also cannot be fixed by "just retry" — the recovery is manual.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After a **refused** local-dev fast-forward (`local_dev_diverged` / `commit_not_based_on_remote_tip`), `finish` retries the fast-forward once it has rebased the commit onto `origin/dev`, so the main checkout's `dev` (and its `HEAD` when `dev` is checked out) is at the pushed commit before the push.
- [ ] If the fast-forward still cannot be taken (main checkout dirty, or local `dev` carries a *different* unpublished commit), `finish` does not push from the main checkout: it either refuses with the actionable holder/divergence detail it already collects, or pushes with cwd = the retained worktree (which is checked out at the commit), so the pushed-commit guard measures the pushed tree.
- [ ] A regression test drives the concurrent-move shape (worktree based on `dev~1`, another commit on `origin/dev`) and asserts that the guard's three preconditions hold at push time: pushed sha == gate tree HEAD, gate tree clean.
- [ ] `finish` reports the guard refusal distinguishably (a `push.refused_by_pushed_commit_guard` step with pushed sha, gate HEAD and gate tree) instead of a generic push failure, and its recovery guidance names the worktree push.

## Notes

- Guard: `.githooks/pre-push` §3a (LP-0MVSJUM3O003C0H9).
- Push cwd: `implement.py` → `git_push_to_dev(repo_root, branch, commit_hash)` (~line 6774).
- The concurrent local-only commit seen in the main checkout that day (`0f153a89`, item LP-0MVUH9OYZ007GMWF) is an independent, expected transient of a sibling session; it is *not* the cause of this refusal and must not be discarded.

## Goal

As the proxy operator I want to know, with evidence, whether the compaction
header bridge (option 2: proxy signals compaction, client mirrors the compacted
view) actually works end to end — and if it does not, to fix the specific
broken link — so that we stop carrying an "implemented" feature that changes
nothing.

`discovered-from: LP-0MTYGZ1DI0004QP8` (producer, completed) and
`SorraAgents:SA-0MTYGZIWF000ZLU0` (client bridge, deleted).

## Why this exists: the bridge has never run

An RCA on 2026-10-31 established that option 2 did not *fail* — it was never
executed. The mechanism is sound; the chain was never completed.

| # | Link | State | Evidence (verified 2026-10-31) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Proxy decides to compact | **DISABLED** | `proxy/config.yaml` `compaction_trigger_ratio: 0`; `proxy/proxy/compaction.py:873` returns `reason="compaction_disabled"` when `trigger <= 0`; 54,937 `compaction_bypass_eval … action=noop reason=compaction_disabled` in retained logs; **0** `action=compact`; usage report "No compactions observed in window" |
| 2 | Proxy emits `X-Compaction-*` | **cannot fire** | `proxy/proxy/router.py:410` gates on `session_result["compaction_applied"]`, set only at `router_helpers.py:5856` when `action=="compact" and applied and not dry_run`; **0** occurrences of the header name in retained logs |
| 3 | Pi surfaces response headers | works | `pi-coding-agent/dist/core/extensions/types.d.ts:707` (`AfterProviderResponseEvent {status, headers}`); Local Proxy uses `api: openai-completions`, whose transport passes `headersToRecord(response.headers)` on SSE responses |
| 4 | Bridge mirrors the view | installed, idle | symlink `~/.pi/agent/extensions/proxy-compaction-bridge` → `~/projects/SorraAgents/pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge` (target present); absent headers ⇒ deliberate no-op by contract |
| 5 | End-to-end validation | **never happened** | the SA audit failed on infrastructure (`audit concurrency queue 'audit' saturated … no slot within 90s`, model output unparseable), recorded 8/8 ACs "partial", then the item was deleted; no gap item was raised |

Timeline defect: the bridge was implemented and symlinked **2026-09-17** with the
note *"headers are not yet emitted … live end-to-end validation is pending the
producer side"*; the producer shipped in **v0.1.19 on 2026-09-23**, and
server-side compaction was disabled **the same day** (LP-0MU61IRVC003RRN6).
The overlap in which both halves were live was effectively zero.

## Secondary findings (would bite even with the signal on)

1. **No base handshake.** The contract is one-directional. The client rebuilds
   the base from its own JSONL (`custom_message` entries, `context_edit`
   omissions, tool results the proxy never stored); the proxy rebuilds from its
   own store. On disagreement `session_manager.py:451` sets
   `fallback_reason="history_mismatch"` → full reprocess and CREATION
   re-summarisation, i.e. exactly the churn the bridge exists to remove — and it
   fails **silently**.
2. **No runtime observability.** Header emission logs nothing (`router.py:430`
   is a `debug` on the failure path only) and the bridge logs nothing, so a
   loaded-but-idle extension is indistinguishable from a broken one.
3. **Ruled out:** marker role/shape is consistent on both sides — both use a
   user-role marker (`compaction.py:308`, `compaction-bridge.js:191`) and both
   build `system… + first_user + marker + tail` (`compaction.py:882`).

## Scope

Phase A — **prove the wire contract** (no client involved), then
Phase B — **prove the client mirror**, then
Phase C — **repair** whichever link fails, with the handshake and observability
below. Phase C is conditional on what A/B show; do not implement C speculatively.

In scope:
- Re-enabling the producer for a bounded, single-session probe and observing the
  four headers on a real response.
- Permanent INFO telemetry: one line per emission (proxy) and one per capture +
  one per reshape (bridge).
- If (and only if) A or B fails: base identity (`X-Compaction-Base-Id`
  emitted, `X-Dispatch-Base-Id` accepted) so divergence is detected explicitly
  instead of degrading into `history_mismatch`.

Out of scope:
- Pi-side native compaction (`~/.pi/agent/settings.json` `compaction.enabled`),
  which is the alternative, simpler route and a separate decision.
- Re-designing the summariser, compaction thresholds, or `turns_summarized`
  semantics.
- The local→remote boundary compaction hook (LP-0MVTDUBR00038ZRL).

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1 (Phase A): On a dedicated probe session, one response carries
  `X-Compaction-Occurred: true`, `X-Compaction-Marker`,
  `X-Compaction-Turns-Summarized`, `X-Compaction-Recent-Turns-Kept`, and the
  base64 marker decodes verbatim to the message the proxy injected (including
  the `The conversation history before this point was compacted into the
  following summary:` / `</summary>` delimiters). Test procedure T1.
- AC2 (Phase A, isolation): During T1 no session other than the probe session
  emits `compaction_event action=compact`, and the config is restored to
  `compaction_trigger_ratio: 0` before the item is closed. Test procedure T1
  steps 8–9.
- AC3 (Phase B): A live pi session crossing the trigger shows, in order: proxy
  `compaction_event … action=compact` → bridge "signal captured" → bridge
  "reshaped N→M messages" → next proxy request carrying the compacted base with
  **no** `history_mismatch` and **no** from-scratch re-summarisation. Test
  procedure T2.
- AC4 (observability, unconditional): the proxy logs one INFO per header
  emission (session, `turns_summarized`, `recent_turns_kept`, marker length) and
  the bridge logs one line per signal capture and one per reshape. A reader of
  the logs can tell "no signal emitted" from "signal emitted, bridge ignored it".
- AC5 (Phase C, conditional): if the mirrored base diverges, the proxy detects
  it explicitly (base id mismatch, logged) instead of reporting
  `history_mismatch`, and re-signals exactly once; a second consecutive
  divergence stops mirroring for that session and logs why.
- AC6 (regression): with `compaction_trigger_ratio: 0` restored, no
  `X-Compaction-*` header is emitted, no bridge state is created, and the
  existing admission/routing decision path is unchanged (existing compaction and
  admission suites green).
- AC7: The item records a verdict — "option 2 viable" or "option 2 not viable,
  reason X" — with the T1/T2 log excerpts attached, so the earlier
  "implemented but inert" state cannot recur.

## Test instructions

### Preconditions (do not skip)

1. Proxy healthy: `curl -s --max-time 5 http://localhost:8080/v1/models | head -c 200`.
2. Summariser reachable — compaction summarises via
   `summarizer_model: {type: local, llama_model: Qwen2.5-7B}`
   (`proxy/config.yaml:1452`). If it is down, compaction returns
   `action=remote_with_guidance reason=summarizer_failed` and **no headers** are
   emitted; that is a precondition failure, not a bridge failure.
3. Confirm the starting state is disabled:
   `grep -c 'action=compact' /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log` → expect `0`.
4. **Safety:** `compaction_dry_run: false` (`proxy/config.yaml:1477`), so
   raising the ratio goes LIVE, not advisory. Contain the blast radius by
   pinning a dedicated `x-session-id` for the probe (compaction is per-session),
   and restore the ratio immediately after. Do not run this while a release or
   audit batch is in flight.

### T1 — prove the wire contract (deterministic, no pi involved)

1. Compute the trigger for the change you are about to make: with
   `local_model_ctx_size: 262144` and 2 slots, the per-slot clamp is
   `262144 // 2 - 4096 = 126976`; at ratio `0.7` the trigger is
   **88,883 tokens** (`compaction.py:226`). The probe session must exceed it and
   stay under the 120,000 warm routing cap, so target ~100k estimated tokens.
2. Enable the producer: set `compaction_trigger_ratio: 0.7` in
   `proxy/config.yaml`, then
   `curl -sX POST http://localhost:8080/admin/reload-config` → expect
   `{"status":"success",...}` and log line
   `Configuration reloaded successfully via admin endpoint`.
3. Build a 3-turn probe (≥88,883 estimated tokens, <120,000) with a unique
   session id:
   ```bash
   SID="rca-compaction-probe-$(date +%s)"
   python3 - "$SID" <<'PY'
   import json, sys
   sid = sys.argv[1]
   filler = ("RCA probe payload for the compaction header bridge. " * 7000)  # ~420 KB
   msgs = [{"role": "user", "content": filler + "
TURN 1"}]
   for n in (2, 3):
       msgs.append({"role": "assistant", "content": "ack"})
       msgs.append({"role": "user", "content": filler + f"
TURN {n}"})
   body = {"model": "code", "stream": True, "messages": msgs,
           "max_tokens": 16, "temperature": 0}
   open("/tmp/probe.json", "w").write(json.dumps(body))
   open("/tmp/probe.sid", "w").write(sid)
   print("session:", sid, "messages:", len(msgs), "chars:", sum(len(m["content"]) for m in msgs))
   PY
   ```
   Re-send this same body until the session crosses the trigger (the proxy logs
   the estimate per request as `compaction_bypass_eval … est_before=<n>`; check
   it with
   `grep 'compaction_bypass_eval' /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log | tail -1`).
   Sending it twice from the same `x-session-id` is normally enough. Tune the
   `* 7000` multiplier if `est_before` lands outside 89k–119k.
4. Send request N and capture headers:
   ```bash
   curl -sS -N -D /tmp/h_N.txt -o /tmp/body_N.txt \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer not_needed" \
     -H "x-session-id: $(cat /tmp/probe.sid)" \
     -H "x-local-preference: local-preferred" \
     --data @/tmp/probe.json http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions
   ```
5. **Pass criterion A** — the response that compacts carries all four headers:
   ```bash
   grep -i '^x-compaction-' /tmp/h_N.txt
   # expect:
   # x-compaction-occurred: true
   # x-compaction-marker: <base64>
   # x-compaction-turns-summarized: <n≥1>
   # x-compaction-recent-turns-kept: <k>
   ```
6. **Pass criterion B** — the marker round-trips verbatim:
   ```bash
   grep -i '^x-compaction-marker:' /tmp/h_N.txt | cut -d' ' -f2- | base64 -d
   # must start with: The conversation history before this point was compacted into the following summary:
   # and end with:    </summary>
   ```
7. **Pass criterion C** — the proxy agrees it compacted live:
   ```bash
   grep -E 'compaction_event .*action=compact|session_compaction applied' \
        /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log | tail -4
   # expect action=compact, reason=compacted_within_target, dry_run=False,
   # and `session_compaction applied session=$(cat /tmp/probe.sid)`
   ```
   If instead you see `action=noop reason=below_trigger`, the probe is too small
   — go back to step 3. If `action=remote_with_guidance
   reason=summarizer_failed`, the precondition in 2 is broken.
8. Confirm isolation (AC2): `grep 'action=compact' /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log
   | grep -v "$(cat /tmp/probe.sid)"` → expect empty.
9. Restore: `compaction_trigger_ratio: 0`, `curl -sX POST
   …/admin/reload-config`, then confirm the next request logs
   `reason=compaction_disabled` and the response carries no `X-Compaction-*`
   header. Delete the probe session:
   `curl -sX DELETE http://localhost:8080/admin/sessions/$(cat /tmp/probe.sid)`.

**T1 verdict:** if any of A/B/C fails, stop — the producer side is the defect and
Phase C is not needed yet. Record the raw headers and log lines on this item.

### T2 — prove the client mirror (pi session)

1. Add the AC4 logging to the bridge (`pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/`):
   log in `handleResponse` (`signal captured session=… turns_summarized=…
   recent_turns_kept=… marker_chars=…`) and in `reshape` (`reshaped X→Y
   messages for session=…`, plus a no-op line `no signal — passthrough` when
   state is absent). Keep it to one line each, no payload bodies.
2. `/reload` in pi (or restart it). Confirm from pi's own log that the extension
   loaded; a load error here is itself a finding.
3. Start a fresh pi session on `Local Proxy/code`, re-enable the producer as in
   T1 step 2, and work turns until the session crosses 88,883 estimated tokens
   (paste a large file if you need to move fast; watch `est_before` in the proxy
   log).
4. **Pass criterion D** — ordering is visible and correct:
   proxy `compaction_event action=compact` → bridge `signal captured` →
   bridge `reshaped X→Y messages` (Y < X).
5. **Pass criterion E** — the next pi request carries the compacted base:
   in the proxy log the next `routing_estimate_session` / request for that
   session shows the reduced token count, **no** `history_mismatch`, and **no
   second from-scratch** `compaction_event` (incremental only: `turns_summarized`
   should stay small relative to the session, not reset to "everything").
6. **Fail signature to record verbatim** (this is RCA finding F4): any of
   `history_mismatch` on the following turn, `est_before` jumping back up to the
   pre-compaction value, or a repeated `action=compact` whose `turns_summarized`
   equals the whole session — i.e. the client's rebuilt base is not recognised
   as the proxy's base.
7. Restore `compaction_trigger_ratio: 0` and reload.

**T2 verdict:** pass ⇒ option 2 is viable, close with AC7's "viable" record (and
AC5 is not needed). Fail ⇒ Phase C: implement base identity
(`X-Compaction-Base-Id` = hash of the emitted base; client returns it as
`X-Dispatch-Base-Id`; proxy adopts a matching client base instead of
re-summarising, logs a mismatch once, and re-signals once).

## Evidence to attach on closure

- `/tmp/h_N.txt` header dump (redact the marker body, keep its length and the
  decoded first/last line).
- The matching `compaction_event` / `session_compaction applied` lines.
- The T2 bridge lines plus the following request's `est_before` /
  `history_mismatch` evidence.
- The restored-config check (AC6).

## Related

- LP-0MTYGZ1DI0004QP8 (producer — headers), LP-0MU44KSMS002DBWA,
  LP-0MU44KR5F0015D7A (contract tests).
- LP-0MU61IRVC003RRN6 (disabled server-side compaction; reason this is inert).
- LP-0MTXGU9N1009QNSB (compaction not durable across turns),
  LP-0MTXEBQ4E001BMI2 (local HTTP 400 on compacted history).
- SorraAgents SA-0MTYGZIWF000ZLU0 (client bridge, deleted; commits d6def7bb,
  16d2bd0c — code is present at `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/`).
- LP-0MVTDUBR00038ZRL (adjacent boundary-compaction mechanism).

# local_active_queries leaks ~1 increment per 2.6 local requests (136 self-heals in 13 h) — capacity signal under-reports free slots

## Problem statement

The proxy's `local_active_queries` counter drifts **upward** and is repaired by the
self-healing clamp in `_recover_stuck_local_active_queries`
(`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py:5718`), which logs
`local_active_queries counter recovered: reset from N to M (M active dispatch records)`
at WARNING on every repair tick (10 s). That clamp is the documented safety net from
**LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM** (high, completed) — *"False 'saturated' capacity signal starves
herdr downtime dispatcher overnight"* — plus the earlier leak fixes
LP-0MRIL2L3E0080OGC, LP-0MRMGUEVR0002S5W and LP-0MS8ZM98R000M8AN.

The leak is still occurring, at a high rate, on 2026-10-31:

- **136 recovery warnings** between 00:00 and 13:05 (`proxy.log-2026-10-31_00` 18,
  `proxy.log.2026-10-31_00` 60, `proxy.log.2026-10-31_06` 52, `proxy.log` 6).
- Delta distribution: 47× `2→1`, 18× `1→0`, 13× `3→2`, 8× `3→1`/`4→2`/`2→0`
  — i.e. almost always **one increment that was never decremented**.
- Context: **359 local streams** in the same period ⇒ roughly **one leaked increment per
  2.6 local requests** (not a rare race).

## Why it matters (impact chain)

`local_active_queries` is the proxy's in-flight local-request count. It is consumed by:

1. **`/llama/local/status`** — `available_slots`, `capacity_hint`, `active_query`. The
   herdr downtime worker's dispatch gate reads exactly these fields
   (`DOWNTIME_*_MIN_FREE_SLOTS`); an over-count reports `freeSlots: 0` and starves
   dispatch — the LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM symptom, which is why that item existed.
2. **Admission pricing** (`prefill_eta` occupancy) and the admission guard's
   `eta_occupancy_s` / `projected_wait_s`, so an over-count turns an admissible request
   into `eta_exceeds_budget`.
3. **Prefill saturation gating** (`prefill_gate_wait_ms`, `saturation=...`).

Observed in the same window as the parent finding: `12:42:45` and `12:42:55`
`WARNING local_active_queries counter recovered: reset from 3 to 2 (2 active dispatch
records)` while the pool has **2 slots** — the counter claimed three in-flight local
requests on a two-slot server, so admission and any slot reader saw a server that was
busy when it was not.

## Suspected coupling (verify, do not assume)

The measured-cache-deficit abort / eviction machinery is new since
LP-0MVV9JWL9003A6XR ("0 pre-change" for that class) and it releases leases and records
abandoned slots on a path that also ends the request
(`lease_released`, `abandoned_slot_recorded`, `local_eviction … reason=…`). A skipped
`_decrement_local_active_queries` on any of those early-exit paths would produce exactly
this pattern (one leaked increment per aborted request). LP-0MVWEZCB0006WPBQ changes the
same paths, so this must be diagnosed rather than guessed: the item may turn into an AC
there instead of a separate fix.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — **Quantify**: a deterministic analysis over ≥24 h of proxy logs reports the
      recovery-warning count, the delta distribution, and the leak ratio per local stream
      (baseline: 136 warnings / 359 local streams for 2026-10-31 00:00–13:05, deltas 1
      dominant). Recorded as a comment on this item.
- [ ] AC2 — **Locate the leaking path(s)**: identify every early-exit path that ends a
      local request (normal completion, client cancel, deficit abort, eviction,
      no-progress watchdog, tenancy-lease reclaim, slot-assignment free, exception) and
      state for each whether it decrements the counter. Deliver as a table in a comment,
      with `file:line` for each release path.
- [ ] AC3 — **Fix**: every release path decrements exactly once (or the increment is
      moved so it cannot leak). A regression test drives each path and asserts the counter
      returns to its pre-request value — including the deficit-abort/eviction paths.
- [ ] AC4 — **Invariant test**: a concurrency test (≥3 parallel local streams, mixed
      success/abort/cancel) asserts the counter equals the number of active dispatch
      records at every step, so the recovery clamp never fires (assert zero
      `counter recovered` log lines).
- [ ] AC5 — **Observability**: keep the recovery WARNING (it is the detector) and add the
      leaking request's identifying fields (`session`, `turn`, dispatch-record id, release
      reason) to it when known, so a recurrence is diagnosable without a new investigation.
- [ ] AC6 — **Target**: over a ≥60 min post-fix window with real traffic, **0** recovery
      warnings; the 24 h figure recorded in AC1 must not recur. Evidence as a comment.
- [ ] AC7 — Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Do not remove or weaken the self-healing clamp — it is the last line of defence and the
  detector for this class.
- No change to admission pricing or slot-count semantics beyond making the counter
  accurate.
- If AC2 shows the leak is a benign read race in the clamp (not a missed decrement), prove
  it with evidence and downgrade the warning to debug with a documented rationale — either
  way the signal must end up actionable, not permanently noisy.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_increment_local_active_queries` (~2926),
  `_decrement_local_active_queries`, `_recover_stuck_local_active_queries` (~5718),
  `_count_active_local_dispatch_records`.
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` / the release paths (~1418, ~1586).
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — eviction/lease-release and abort early-exits
  (`local_eviction`, `abandoned_slot_recorded`, `lease_released`).
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — `/llama/local/status` payload.
- `proxy/tests/` — new regression + concurrency tests.

## Existing state (verified 2026-10-31)

- Clamp present with `local_active_queries > active_count` comparison; logs at WARNING.
- 136 warnings / 359 local streams in 13 h; deltas almost always 1.
- Prior related (all completed): LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM, LP-0MRIL2L3E0080OGC,
  LP-0MRMGUEVR0002S5W, LP-0MS8ZM98R000M8AN, LP-0MSAO0ZM4000QH3O.
- `wl search local_active_queries` → no open item covers the recurrence.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVWEZCB0006WPBQ** (critical) — deficit-abort 503 quarantines the whole
  `local-qwen3` entry; shares the eviction/abort release paths where this leak may live.
- **LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM** (high, completed) — the false-saturated signal + this clamp.
- **LP-0MVV9JWL9003A6XR** — eviction triage for the new `measured_cache_deficit` class.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — double decrement.** Tightening one path can double-release elsewhere; the
  AC4 invariant test must cover mixed paths, not just the fixed one.
- **Assumption.** The clamp's `active_count` (dispatch records) is the correct ground
  truth. If records are themselves created late, the clamp can undercount and reset a
  genuinely busy counter — AC2 must confirm the record/counter ordering explicitly.

## Review update (2026-10-31, independent proxy-log review — session `herdr-1793450762-1330301-22426`)

### AC1 baseline correction (measured, reproducible)

Recount over every timestamped 2026-10-31 log file
(`proxy.log.2026-10-31_003749`, `_004152`, `_00`, `_06`, live `proxy.log`; 00:00 → 13:14):

| file | `local_active_queries counter recovered` |
|---|---|
| `proxy.log.2026-10-31_003749` (00:00–00:37) | 2 |
| `proxy.log.2026-10-31_004152` (00:37–00:41) | 0 |
| `proxy.log.2026-10-31_00` (00:41–06:41) | 37 |
| `proxy.log.2026-10-31_06` (06:42–12:41) | 32 |
| `proxy.log` (12:42–13:14) | 5 |
| **total** | **76** |
